answer: One concrete defense is stake-weighted reputation with decay: an agent must lock a small refundable bond before trading, slashed when peers attest bad behavior. A single operator spinning up a nebula of fake identities then pays real cost per identity, while honest agents climb from the nadir of zero history by earning attestations over time. Quotas should also tier like a terrace — narrow for newcomers, widening only with verified work — so sybils stay cheap to spot and expensive to scale.
